summary: Makes King’s Beyond Course offer more visible, navigable and evidence-led by establishing King’s Edge as its common shopfront and creating a live institutional view of participation, reach and impact.
detailSummary:
King’s already provides a rich range of opportunities beyond the course and has developed both a functioning King’s Edge platform and a substantial evidence base about student participation. This deliverable brings those foundations together into a more coherent institutional system.

It will establish King’s Edge as the common shopfront for significant Beyond Course opportunity, progressively bringing service, faculty and institution-wide provision into one navigable student-facing environment. It will set the business requirements for how opportunities are described, categorised, curated and connected to students’ wider educational journeys, working through the Digital Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product development rather than creating a separate digital solution.

Alongside this, it will turn existing baselining work into a live Beyond Course dashboard, combining current provider data with increasingly automated participation data from King’s Edge. Staff will be able to move from an institutional picture of engagement through individual services, programmes and activities, understand who is and is not participating, and use common measures to evaluate reach and equity.

The evidence model will deepen over time to examine the relationship between participation and outcomes including career readiness, academic success, self-efficacy, belonging and engagement. Major investments and strategically significant programmes will be subject to more focused evaluation, helping King’s build greater confidence about the value its Beyond Course investment creates for students.

By bringing visibility and evidence together, King’s will be better able to improve provision, address gaps and inequalities, strengthen successful activity and make more confident decisions about future investment.
problemSolved: King’s has substantial Beyond Course provision, a functioning opportunity platform and a growing evidence base, but these do not yet operate as one institutional system. Significant provision remains dispersed across local channels, participation evidence is not yet routinely available to providers and leaders through a live common dashboard, and King’s cannot consistently connect the scale of its investment to reach, equity and student impact.
whatChanges: King’s establishes a visible, evidence-led Beyond Course offer. Significant opportunities are progressively shopfronted through King’s Edge, staff gain a live institutional dashboard of participation and reach, impact analysis becomes more systematic, and the resulting evidence is used to improve provision and inform investment decisions.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s already invests significantly in opportunities beyond the course, delivered through services, faculties and institution-wide programmes spanning careers and employability, volunteering, academic and research opportunities, skills development, libraries, entrepreneurship, culture, community and other forms of student participation. Over recent years, King’s has also developed a growing institutional evidence base about this activity and established the King’s Edge platform as a functioning route through which opportunities can be presented to students.

These foundations are not yet operating as a coherent institutional system. Significant parts of the Beyond Course offer remain dispersed across local websites, booking systems, communications and provider networks. Students therefore have an uneven view of what is available to them, while King’s cannot yet be confident that the full breadth of its investment is visible and navigable through a common student-facing shopfront.

Our understanding of participation is similarly fragmented. Existing baselining work and provider data give King’s a substantial starting point, but much of this evidence is assembled periodically and returned inconsistently to the services that generate it. We can describe significant volumes of activity, but cannot yet routinely move from an institutional picture to individual providers and opportunities, understand who is and is not participating, or compare participation with wider measures of student development and success.

As a result, King’s does not yet have a sufficiently live or consistent basis for understanding the reach, equity and impact of its Beyond Course investment, nor for making confident decisions about what should be sustained, improved, grown or reconsidered.
caseForChange.opportunity:
King’s can now build on the infrastructure and evidence already created to establish a coherent institutional view of the Beyond Course experience.

A live Beyond Course dashboard can bring existing provider data together with an increasing flow of participation data from King’s Edge, allowing staff to move from the whole institutional picture through individual services, programmes and activities. Common measures of reach and participation can be combined with deeper evaluation of outcomes including career readiness, academic success, self-efficacy, belonging and engagement. For major institutional investments, this creates the opportunity to move towards a much stronger account of the value generated for students.

At the same time, King’s can establish King’s Edge as the common shopfront for significant Beyond Course opportunity. Rather than students needing to understand which organisational unit provides an opportunity or where that provider happens to advertise it, the institution can progressively bring its offer into one navigable environment, supported by common expectations for how opportunities are described, categorised and connected to students' wider educational journeys.

Together, these developments create a virtuous relationship between visibility and evidence: a more complete digital shopfront generates richer institutional participation data, while better evidence helps King’s improve the offer, its presentation and the investments that sit behind it.
caseForChange.whyNow:
The foundations for this shift are already in place. King’s has undertaken substantial work to baseline Beyond Course participation and already holds data from a wide range of providers that can now be turned rapidly into a useful institutional reporting product. The immediate opportunity is to move this from periodic analysis into a live Power BI dashboard during 2026, with increasingly automated data feeds as the underlying digital infrastructure matures.

King’s Edge is also already a live opportunity platform. Its planned replatforming provides an important technical foundation, but the more significant institutional challenge is now adoption: ensuring that services, faculties and major programmes consistently use the platform so that students can encounter a genuinely rich representation of the King’s Beyond Course offer in one place.

The wider development of the Digital Student Experience Hub makes this particularly timely. Decisions are being made now about the future King’s Edge product, its data structures, pathways, provider spaces, discovery journeys and analytics. The Beyond Course proposition therefore needs a clear business owner able to set institutional requirements and ensure those developments serve a coherent student experience rather than simply recreating existing fragmentation in a new technical environment.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s establishes a visible, evidence-led Beyond Course offer that can be understood and navigated by students and actively stewarded by the institution.

Significant Beyond Course opportunities are progressively shopfronted through King’s Edge using common institutional expectations for description, categorisation and student navigation. Students gain a clearer view of the opportunities available beyond their course and how these can contribute to their interests, development and wider King’s experience.

Staff gain a live Beyond Course dashboard that provides a common view of participation and reach, with the ability to move from institutional patterns into services, programmes and individual activities. Over time, this is supplemented by stronger analysis of who participates and the relationship between participation and outcomes such as career readiness, academic success, self-efficacy, belonging and engagement.

This evidence becomes part of how King’s manages its Beyond Course portfolio. Providers can understand and improve their own reach and impact, leaders can identify inequalities, gaps and duplication, and major investments can be tested more confidently against the value they create for students. King’s moves towards an institutional expectation that significant Beyond Course activity should be both visible to students and visible in the evidence used to understand and improve the student experience.
